**Naming of the Surah**

• It is called al-Ma'idah (the Table Spread), because it includes the story of the descent of the table (al-ma'idah) upon the companions of the Prophet of Allah, Jesus, peace be upon him. It is the only surah that speaks of the disciples' request to their prophet Jesus that he ask his Lord to send down a table from heaven, which would be a day of festivity for them and for those who would come after them.

**Some of the Objectives of the Surah**

• Explaining a number of legal rulings, such as the command to fulfill contracts, the rulings on food and hunting, marriage to women of the People of the Book, purification from ritual impurity (hadath), and mention of some penal laws, such as retaliation (qisas) for lives and limbs, the expiation for breaking an oath, and the prohibition of wine and gambling (maysir). It also mentions some customs of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period of ignorance), such as seeking decisions by arrows (al-istiqsam bil-azlam), and the prohibition of certain kinds of cattle (bahimat al-an'am), along with other rulings.

• Guidance to preserve the rites of Allah during the Hajj, in the sacred month, and while in a state of ihram, and the command to be just in judgment, even with enemies, and its application by being fair to the Christians in what is due to them, those who are characterized by worship, humility and tenderness of heart, and that they are closer to accepting Islam.

• Explaining the principles of dealing between Muslims and the People of the Book, the polytheists and the hypocrites, and warning against allying with them, and explaining a number of the bad moral traits of the Jews, and implicitly warning against these traits, such as breaking covenants, killing the prophets, treachery and deceit, and consuming unlawful gain (al-suht).

• Explaining a number of the misguidances of the Jews and Christians, such as the explanation of their false beliefs about Allah, His attributes and His prophets, their distortion of their scriptures, their neglect of the Sharia, their exaggeration in religion, their disbelief in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), their obstinacy in responding to their prophets, and their silence about sins until evil spread among them, for which they deserved the curse and wrath.

• Training souls to accept the truth, by explaining the methods of the people of falsehood with their prophets and the characteristics of the evil soul, through a number of stories, and pointing to the struggle between good and evil, where the surah mentions a model of the evil soul and a model of the good soul, represented in the story of the two sons of Adam.

• Reminding of the Day of Resurrection, glorifying Allah, the Exalted, in a manner appropriate to that situation, and mentioning the testimony of Jesus against the Christians on that day.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, fulfill the covenants of Allah that are binding, from belief in the laws of the religion and submission to them, and fulfill the covenants you make with one another regarding trusts, sales and other matters, provided they do not contradict the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah has permitted you the beast of cattle, namely camels, cows and sheep, except what He has made clear to you of the prohibition of carrion, blood and other things, and the prohibition of hunting while you are in ihram for Hajj or Umrah, or while you are within the Sacred Precinct (al-haram). Indeed, Allah judges as He wills, in accordance with His wisdom and justice.

O you who have believed, God and His Messenger, and act according to His law: do not violate the limits of God and His markers (ma'alim). Do not make lawful fighting in the sacred months, which are: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram and Rajab, and this was in the early days of Islam. Do not make lawful the sanctity of the sacrificial animals (al-hady), nor those that have been marked with garlands, for they used to place garlands (al-qala'id), which are plaited strands of wool or camel hair placed on the necks as a sign that the animal is a sacrificial offering and that the man intends the Hajj. Do not make lawful fighting against those who head for the Sacred House, who seek bounty from God and His good pleasure that would sustain their livelihoods and please their Lord. When you have come out of your state of ihram, hunting becomes lawful for you. Let not hatred of a people, because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, as happened in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, lead you to abandon justice towards them. Cooperate, O believers, among yourselves in doing good and in piety toward God, and do not cooperate in what contains sin, disobedience and transgression of God's limits. Beware of opposing God's command, for indeed He is severe in punishment.

Allah has forbidden you carrion, which is an animal whose life has departed without proper slaughter (dhakah). He has also forbidden you flowing blood that is poured out, the flesh of swine, and that over which a name other than Allah's has been invoked at slaughter; the strangled (al-munkhaniqah), which is one whose breath has been held until it dies; the beaten (al-mawqudhah), which is one struck with a stick or stone until it dies; the fallen (al-mutaraddiyah), which is one that has fallen from a high place or plunged into a well and died; the gored (al-nati'ah), which is one that another animal has struck with its horn until it dies. Allah has also forbidden you an animal that a predator has eaten, such as the lion, the leopard, the wolf, and the like. Exempted by Him, glorified is He, from what He has forbidden of the strangled and what follows it is that which you reached in time to slaughter (dhakah) before it died; it is lawful for you. Allah has forbidden you that which is slaughtered for other than Allah, upon what is set up for worship, such as a stone or other than it. Allah has forbidden you to seek to know what has been apportioned to you or not apportioned by means of the arrows (al-azlam), which are the divining arrows (al-qidah) with which they used to seek the decision when they wanted a matter before proceeding with it. That which is mentioned in the verse of the prohibited things, if they are committed, is a departure from the command of Allah and obedience to Him toward disobedience to Him. Today the hopes of the disbelievers have been cut off from your religion, that you would revert from it to polytheism after I have granted you victory over them, so do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected for you your religion, Islam, by achieving victory and completing the law, and I have completed My favor upon you by bringing you out of the darknesses of the Jahiliyyah into the light of faith, and I have approved Islam as a religion for you, so adhere to it and do not depart from it. Whoever is compelled by severe hunger to eat carrion, while not deliberately inclining toward sin, then it is permissible for him to eat it, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful toward him.

They ask you, O Prophet, about what has been made lawful for them to eat. Say to them: What is good and wholesome has been made lawful for you, and so has the game caught by what you have trained from among the animals with claws and fangs, such as dogs, leopards, and falcons, and the like of what can be taught. You teach them to hunt for you, of what Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah when you release them to hunt. And fear Allah in what He has commanded you and in what He has forbidden you. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.

And among the completion of Allah's blessing upon you today, O believers, is that He has made lawful for you the good things. The slaughtered animals of the Jews and Christians, if they slaughter them according to their law, are lawful for you, and your slaughtered animals are lawful for them. He has also made lawful for you, O believers, marriage to the muhsanat (chaste women), namely free women among the believing women who are chaste and abstain from unlawful intercourse (zina). Likewise, marriage to free chaste women from among the Jews and Christians is lawful, provided you give them their dowries (mahr), and you are chaste yourselves, not committing zina and not taking paramours, and you are secure from being influenced by their religion. Whoever denies the laws of faith, his deed has become void, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be among the losers.

O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows (والمِرْفَق: al-mirfaq, the joint that lies between the forearm and the upper arm), wipe over your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles (وهما العظمان البارزان عند ملتقى الساق بالقدم: al-ka'bayn, the two bones that protrude at the juncture of the shin and the foot). And if you are in a state of major impurity, then purify yourselves by bathing before prayer. And if you are sick, or on a journey, or one of you has relieved himself, or you have had contact with women, and you find no water, then strike the earth with your hands and wipe your faces and your hands with it. Allah does not intend to place any hardship upon you in matters of purification, but rather He has permitted tayammum (dry ablution, tayammum) as a facilitation for you and as a mercy to you, for He has made it a substitute for water in purification. Thus the concession of tayammum is among the complete blessings which call for thanks to the Bestower, by obeying Him in what He commanded and in what He forbade.

And remember Allah's blessing upon you in what He has legislated for you, and remember His covenant which He took from you: to believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and to hear and obey them both. Fear Allah regarding what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what you conceal within your souls.

O you who have believed, be steadfast in upholding justice for the sake of Allah, witnesses in fairness. Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just, whether toward enemies or loved ones, on an equal footing; for that justice is closer to God-consciousness. And beware of acting unjustly. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do, and He will recompense you for it.
God promised those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and do righteous deeds that He will forgive their sins and reward them with Paradise for that. Allah does not break His promise.
Those who denied the Oneness of God, which points to the clear truth, and who rejected His signs that the messengers brought, they are the people of the Fire, who will abide in it forever.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, remember the blessing Allah has bestowed upon you: the blessing of security, and the casting of terror into the hearts of your enemies who wanted to strike at you. Allah turned them away from you and came between them and what they intended against you. Fear Allah and beware of Him, and put your trust in Allah alone in your affairs, both religious and worldly, and be confident of His help and His victory.

And Allah had certainly taken a binding covenant from the Children of Israel that they would devote worship to Him alone. Allah commanded Musa to appoint twelve leaders (ʿurafāʾ, sing. ʿarīf) over them, according to the number of their tribes, who would take from them a pledge to hear and obey Allah, His Messenger, and His Book. Allah said to the Children of Israel: "Indeed, I am with you by My protection and My help, if you establish the prayer, give the obligatory zakat to its deserving recipients, believe in My messengers in what they tell you and support them, and spend in My cause. I will certainly remove your misdeeds from you, and I will certainly admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, beneath their palaces and trees. Whoever among you denies this covenant has indeed deviated from the right path to the way of error."

Because of these Jews' breaking of their solemn covenants, We cast them away from Our mercy and made their hearts hard, not softening to faith. They distort the words of Allah which He sent down to Moses, namely the Torah, and they abandoned a portion of what they had been reminded of, so they did not act upon it. And you, O Messenger, will not cease to find among the Jews treachery and deceit, for they follow the path of their forefathers, except for a few of them. So pardon their mistreatment of you, and overlook it, for Allah loves those who excel in pardoning and forgiving toward one who has wronged them. (Thus do people of deviation find a way to their evil aims by distorting the words of Allah and interpreting them other than as intended; and if they fail at distortion and interpretation, they abandon whatever does not accord with their desires of the law of Allah, which only a few stand firm upon, those whom Allah has protected from them.)

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 14:

And We took a covenant from those who claim to be followers of the Messiah, Jesus (peace be upon him) — though they are not such — and it was the firm covenant We had taken from the Children of Israel: that they would follow their messenger, support him, and assist him. But they altered their religion and abandoned a portion of what they had been reminded of, so they did not act upon it, just as the Jews did. Therefore We stirred up enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do on the Day of Reckoning, and He will requite them for their deeds.

O People of the Book, from among the Jews and the Christians, there has come to you Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), who makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal from people from what is in the Torah and the Gospel, and who leaves aside the clarification of much that wisdom does not call for clarifying. There has come to you from God a light and a clear Book: it is the noble Qur'an.

Allah guides by means of this clear Book those who follow His pleasure to the paths of security and safety, and He brings them out by His permission from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith, and He grants them success in His upright religion.

Surely they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, God is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, [O Messenger], to these ignorant Christians: If the Messiah were a god as they claim, he would have been able to avert God's decree when it comes to destroy him, his mother, and everyone on earth altogether. Yet his mother has died, and he did not avert death from her. Likewise, he cannot avert it from himself, because they are both servants of God who have no power to avert destruction from themselves. This is evidence that he is a human being like all the children of Adam. All that exists in the heavens and the earth belongs to God; He creates what He wills and brings it into being, and He is Most Capable of everything. The reality of tawhid (monotheism) necessitates that God, exalted is He, is singular in the attributes of lordship and divinity, so none of His creation shares with Him in that. Frequently, people fall into shirk (associating partners with God) and misguidance by exaggerating regarding the prophets and the righteous, just as the Christians exaggerated regarding the Messiah. So the whole universe belongs to God, creation is in His hand alone, and whatever extraordinary signs and miracles appear return to God. He, glory be to Him, creates what He wills and does what He desires.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 18:

The Jews and the Christians claim that they are the sons of God and His beloved. Say to them, O Messenger: Why then does He punish you for your sins? Had you been His beloved, He would not have punished you. God loves only those who obey Him. Say also to them: Rather, you are creatures like the rest of the children of Adam. If you do good, you will be rewarded with good for your good deeds, and if you do evil, you will be requited with evil for your evil deeds. God forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. He is the Owner of the Kingdom, who disposes of it as He wills, and to Him is the return, so He will judge among His servants and recompense each one according to what he deserves.

O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), making clear to you the truth and the guidance after a interval of time between his sending and the sending of Jesus son of Mary, lest you say: "There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner." So there is now no excuse for you after his being sent to you, for there has come to you from Allah a Messenger who gives good tidings to whoever believes in him and warns whoever disobeys him. And Allah is Able over everything, including the punishment of the disobedient and the reward of the obedient.

Remember, O Messenger, when Moses said to his people: "O Children of Israel, remember the blessing of Allah upon you, when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings, possessing your own affairs, after you had been subjugated to Pharaoh and his people. He has granted you kinds of blessings that He has not granted to anyone else of the worlds of your time."

O my people, enter the Holy Land, that is, the purified land, which is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and what surrounds it, which Allah has promised you that you will enter and fight those in it who are disbelievers. Do not turn back from fighting the tyrants, lest you lose the good of this world and the good of the Hereafter.

They said: "O Musa, indeed in it are a people of great strength and power. We have no ability to fight them, and we will never be able to enter it while they are in it. If they leave it, then we will enter."

Two men from among those who fear Allah, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour by obedience to Him and to His Prophet, said to the Children of Israel: "Enter upon these tyrants through their city gate, taking the means (by acting on the causes). When you enter through the gate, you will overcome them. And upon Allah alone put your trust, if you are true believers in His Messenger in what he has brought you, acting by his law."

The people of Moses said to him: "We will never enter the city as long as they (the tyrants) are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight them; as for us, we will remain sitting here and will not fight them." This was their persistence in disobeying Moses, peace be upon him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 25:

Musa turned to his Lord in supplication, saying: "My Lord, I have no power over anyone except myself and my brother, so decide between us and this rebellious people."

God said to His Prophet Musa (peace be upon him): "Indeed, the Holy Land is forbidden to these Jews to enter for forty years; they will wander about the earth in bewilderment. So do not grieve, O Musa, over the people who have deviated from My obedience."

Recite to the Children of Israel, O Messenger, the account of the two sons of Adam, Qabil and Habil, and it is a true account: when each of them offered a sacrifice, which is that by which one draws near to Allah, the Exalted, Allah accepted the sacrifice of Habil because he was righteous (taqiyy), and did not accept the sacrifice of Qabil because he was not righteous. So Qabil envied his brother and said: "I will surely kill you." Habil replied: "Allah accepts only from those who fear Him."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 28:

Habil (Abel) said, admonishing his brother: "If you stretch your hand out to me to kill me, I will not stretch my hand out to you to kill you, for I fear Allah, the Lord of all the worlds."
﴿Indeed, I want you to bear the sin of my killing and your own sin, and so you will be among the companions of the Fire, abiding therein eternally. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾
So his soul made the killing of his brother seem good to Qabil, and he killed him, and he became one of the losers, those who sold their Hereafter for their worldly life.

When Qabil (Cain) killed his brother, he did not know what to do with his body. So God sent a crow that dug a pit in the earth and buried a dead crow in it, to show Qabil how to bury his brother's corpse. Qabil was amazed and said: "Am I too incapable to do what this crow has done, and cover my brother's nakedness?" So Qabil buried his brother, and God punished him with remorse after he had returned in loss.

Because of this crime of killing, We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul without cause of retribution (qisas), or corruption on the earth in any of the kinds of corruption that necessitate killing, such as polytheism (shirk) and waging war (muharabah), it is as if he had killed all mankind, in terms of the great punishment from Allah that he deserves. And whoever refrains from killing a soul that Allah has forbidden, it is as if he had given life to all mankind; for preserving the sanctity of one person is preserving the sanctities of all people. Our messengers came to the Children of Israel with proofs and evidences for the truth of what they called them to, namely faith in their Lord and fulfilling what was enjoined upon them. Then, after the messengers came to them, most of them still transgress the limits of Allah by committing what Allah has forbidden and abandoning His commands.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 33:

Indeed, the punishment of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, who oppose Him with enmity, who transgress against His rulings and the rulings of His Messenger, and who cause corruption on the earth by killing souls and seizing property, is that they be killed, or crucified along with being killed [crucifixion (al-salb): that the offender is tied to a wooden post], or that the right hand and left foot of the warrior be cut off, or that they be banished from their land to another land, and be imprisoned in a prison of that land until their repentance becomes evident. And this punishment, which Allah has prepared for those who wage war, is a humiliation in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a severe torment if they do not repent.

But those among the fighters who repent before you gain power over them and come back willingly and regretful, then the rights of God that were due from them are dropped. So know, O believers, that God is Forgiving to His servants and Merciful toward them.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, fear Allah, draw near to Him through obedience and by doing what pleases Him, and strive in His cause, so that you may succeed and attain His Gardens.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 36:

Indeed, those who disbelieved in the Oneness of Allah and in His law—even if they possessed everything on earth, and the like of it along with it, and wished to ransom themselves from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection with it, it would not be accepted from them. And for them is a painful punishment.
They want to leave the Fire because of its horrors, but there is no way for them to do so, and theirs is a lasting punishment.

And as for the male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands, O rulers, in accordance with the Shari'ah (divine law). This is a recompense for them for taking people's wealth without right, and a punishment by which God deters others from doing the like of what they did. God is Mighty in His dominion, Wise in His commands and prohibitions.

This is a commentary passage on Qur'an 5:39. Translating the text as given:

Whoever repents after his theft and makes amends in all his actions, then indeed Allah will accept his repentance. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving to His servants, Most Merciful to them.

Did you not know, O Messenger, that Allah is the Creator of the universe, its Manager, and its Owner, and that He, exalted is He, is the Doer of whatever He wills: He punishes whom He wills and forgives whomever He wills, and He is over all things Omnipotent.

O Messenger, do not let grieve you those who race to disbelieve, among the hypocrites who show Islam while their hearts are empty of it. Indeed I will give you victory over them. And do not let grieve you the haste of the Jews to deny your prophethood, for they are a people who listen to falsehood and accept what their rabbis fabricate, and they respond to other people who do not attend your assembly. These others distort the words of Allah after they had understood them, and they say: "If there comes to you from Muhammad what agrees with what we have altered and distorted of the rulings of the Torah, then act upon it; and if there comes to you from him what contradicts it, then beware of accepting it and acting upon it." And whomever Allah wills to be misguided, you, O Messenger, cannot repel that from him, nor can you guide him. Indeed, these hypocrites and Jews, Allah did not intend to purify their hearts from the filth of disbelief. For them is disgrace and humiliation in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.

These Jews combine listening to falsehood with consuming what is forbidden. If they come to you seeking judgment, then judge between them, or leave them alone. If you do not judge between them, they will not be able to harm you in any way. And if you do judge, then judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who are just.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 43:

How strange is the conduct of these Jews! They come to you, O Messenger, for judgment, yet they do not believe in you or in your Book, even though the Torah, which they profess to believe in, is in their possession and contains the judgment of God. Then they turn away after your judgment if it does not please them. Thus they combine disbelief in their own law with turning away from your judgment. Those who display such characteristics are not believers in God, in you, or in what you judge.

Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which there is guidance away from misguidance and an explanation of the rulings. By it the prophets, who submitted to the judgment of God and affirmed it, judged among the Jews. They did not depart from its rulings nor distort it. It was also applied by the worshippers (ʿubbād) and jurists (fuqahāʾ) of the Jews, who guided people by the law of God. That is because their prophets had entrusted them with conveying the Torah and with understanding the Book of God and acting upon it. The rabbis (rabbāniyyūn) and the scholars (aḥbār) were witnesses that their prophets had judged among the Jews by the Book of God. God says to the scholars and rabbis of the Jews: So do not fear people in implementing My judgment, for they cannot benefit you or harm you, but fear Me, for I am the One who benefits and harms. And do not take a paltry price in exchange for abandoning the ruling of what I have sent down. Judging by other than what God has sent down is the deed of the people of disbelief. As for those who alter the ruling of God that He sent down in His Book, concealing it and denying it, and judging by other than it while believing its permissibility, they are the disbelievers.

And We prescribed for them in the Torah: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and wounds are subject to retaliation. Whoever forgoes his right of retaliation against the transgressor, that is an expiation for some of the sins of the one who was wronged, and a removal of them. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed concerning retribution and other matters, then those are the transgressors against the limits of Allah.

Following in their footsteps, We sent Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was in the Torah before him, and acting upon what remained of its rulings that had not been abrogated by his own Book. We gave him the Gospel, containing guidance to the truth and clarifying for people some of the rulings of God that they had been ignorant of, and confirming the truth of the Torah with its rulings that it contained. And We made it a clear guidance and a deterrent for those who fear God, restraining them from committing what is forbidden.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 47:

Let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah revealed in it. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiant ones who have departed from His command and disobeyed Him.

Revealed to you (O Messenger) is the Qur'an, and all of it is truth, bearing witness to the truthfulness of the Scriptures before it and that they are from God, confirming what is sound in them and clarifying what has been distorted in them, and abrogating (naskh) some of their laws. So judge between those among the Jews who come to you for judgment by what God has revealed to you in this Qur'an, and do not turn away from the truth that God has commanded you to follow toward their desires and what they have become accustomed to. "For We have made for every community a law (shari'ah) and a clear way (minhaj) by which they act." Had God willed, He would have made your laws one; but He varied them in order to test you, so that the obedient is distinguished from the disobedient. So race toward what is better for you in both abodes, by acting upon what is in the Qur'an, for your return is to God, and He will inform you of what you used to differ about, and will recompense each one for his deeds.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 49:

So judge, O Messenger, between the Jews by what Allah has sent down to you in the Qur'an, and do not follow their desires, those who come to you for judgment. Beware of them lest they turn you away from some of what Allah has sent down to you, so that you abandon acting upon it. But if these people turn away from what you judge, then know that Allah wills to turn them away from guidance, because of sins they had committed before. Indeed, many of the people are certainly defiant of the obedience of their Lord.

Do these Jews want you to judge between them by what the idolaters, the worshippers of idols, have customarily followed of misguidance and ignorance?! That cannot be, and it is never fitting. And who is more just than Allah in judgment for a people who understand His law, believe in it, and are certain that Allah's judgment is the truth?

O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies and supporters against the people of faith. That is because they do not take the believers as friends. The Jews support one another, and likewise the Christians, and both groups unite in enmity toward you. And you, O believers, are more worthy that some of you support one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies becomes one of them, and his ruling is their ruling. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoers who take the disbelievers as allies.

Allah the Exalted informs us about a group of the hypocrites who were quick to show friendship to the Jews, because of the doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts. They would say: "We only befriend them out of fear that a reversal of fortune might befall us, and they might strike us along with them." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest﴾ — that is, the conquest of Makkah — ﴿or a decision from Him,﴾ and will support His Prophet and make Islam and the Muslims prevail over the disbelievers, or will arrange affairs in such a way that the power of the Jews and Christians is brought to an end, so that they submit to the Muslims. Then the hypocrites will regret what they had concealed within themselves of their friendship with them.

Then some of the believers will say to one another, in wonder at the state of the hypocrites when their affair is exposed: "Are these the ones who swore by their most emphatic oaths that they were truly with you?" The deeds the hypocrites did in this world are nullified, so there is no reward for them for them, because they did those deeds without faith, and so they lost both this world and the Hereafter.

O you who have believed, whoever among you turns back from his religion, [if he does], then Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah and not fearing the blame of any blamer. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
Indeed, your supporter is only Allah, His Messenger, and the believers who maintain the prescribed prayer, give zakat willingly from their own selves, and are humbly submissive to Allah.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the simplified exegesis") on surah 5, verse 56:

Whoever puts his trust in Allah and takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies, then he is of the party of Allah, and the party of Allah are the ones who will prevail and be victorious.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not take as allies those who mock and make a game of your religion, whether from the People of the Scripture or the disbelievers, and fear Allah if you are truly believers in Him and in His law.

And when your caller to prayer calls the adhan, O believers, the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists mock it and ridicule your call to it; this is because of their ignorance of their Lord, and because they do not comprehend the true nature of worship.

Say, O Messenger, to these mockers from the People of the Book: What you find as a criticism or a fault against us is actually a praiseworthy quality for us: our belief in God and in the Books He sent down to us and to those before us, and our belief that most of you are deviating from the straight path!

Say, [O Prophet], to the believers: Shall I inform you of those who will receive a worse recompense on the Day of Resurrection than these deviators?

[The commentary]

They are their forefathers, whom Allah banished from His mercy and against whom He was angry, and whose forms He transformed, making of them apes and swine, because of their disobedience, their slander, and their arrogance. Among them were also those who worshipped the taghut [i.e., everything that is worshipped besides Allah while being content with that worship]. Evil is their abode in the Hereafter, and their striving in this world went astray from the right path.

When they come to you, believers, the hypocrites among the Jews say, "We believe," yet they remain upon their disbelief. They entered among you with the disbelief they hold in their hearts, and they left while still persisting in it. God knows best what they conceal, even though they display the opposite.

You see, O Messenger, many of the Jews hastening to sin: speaking falsehood and lies, transgressing against the commands of Allah, and consuming people's wealth unjustly. Truly evil is what they have been doing, and evil is their transgression.

Why do their leaders and scholars not forbid these people, who race to sin and transgression, from speaking falsehood and false witness, and from consuming people's wealth unjustly? Their conduct is indeed evil, since they abandoned forbidding what is wrong.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 64:

Allah informs His Prophet of some of the sins of the Jews, which they used to conceal among themselves: they said, "The hand of Allah is restrained from doing good; He has been stingy toward us with provision and abundance," and this was when drought and famine struck them. "Their hands were chained" (ghullat aydihim), meaning their own hands were restrained from doing good, and Allah expelled them from His mercy because of their saying. The matter is not as they slander their Lord; rather, His hands are outstretched, none can restrict Him, and nothing prevents Him from giving, for He is the Most Generous, the Most Bountiful, who spends in accordance with wisdom and what serves the welfare of His servants. Yet they will certainly increase in transgression and disbelief because of their malice and envy, since Allah has chosen you for the message. Allah, the Exalted, informs us that the groups of the Jews will continue, until the Day of Resurrection, to be hostile to one another and to keep apart from one another; whenever they plot to scheme against the Muslims by inciting strife and kindling the fire of war, Allah foils their scheme and scatters their unity. The Jews will continue to act in disobedience to Allah, from which corruption and disorder arise upon the earth. And Allah does not love the corrupters.

In the verse is an affirmation of the attribute of two hands for Allah, the Exalted, in a manner befitting Him, without likening Him to anything and without specifying its modality (takyif).

If the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, had believed in Allah and His Messenger, and carried out Allah's commands and avoided His prohibitions, We would have expiated their sins from them and admitted them into the Gardens of Bliss in the Hereafter.

Had they truly acted upon what is in the Torah and the Gospel, and upon what has been revealed to you, O Messenger, meaning the Noble Qur'an, they would have been provided for from every direction. We would have sent down rain upon them and caused fruit to grow for them, and this is the reward of the worldly life. Among the People of the Book, there is a moderate group, steadfast upon the truth, but many of them, their deeds are evil, and they have strayed from the right path.

O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. If you fall short in conveying it and conceal any part of it, then you have not conveyed the message of your Lord. He (ﷺ) conveyed the message of his Lord in full, so whoever claims that he concealed anything of what was revealed to him has committed a great slander against Allah and His Messenger. Allah the Exalted is your protector and your helper against your enemies, so your duty is only to convey. Indeed, Allah does not guide to right guidance those who deviate from the path of truth and deny what you have brought from Allah.

Say, O Messenger, to the Jews and the Christians: "You are not standing on any ground of the religion as long as you do not act upon what is in the Torah and the Gospel, and what has come to you from Muhammad (ﷺ) of the Qur'an." And indeed, many of the People of the Book increase in nothing from the sending down of the Qur'an to you except arrogant defiance and denial. So they envy you, because Allah sent you with this final message, in which He exposed their faults. So do not grieve, O Messenger, over their denial of you.

Indeed, those who believed (meaning the Muslims), and the Jews, and the Sabians likewise (they are a people who remain upon their natural disposition, having no established religion that they follow), and the Christians (they are the followers of the Messiah), whoever among them believed in Allah with complete faith, which is the affirmation of Allah's oneness and the acceptance of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought, and believed in the Last Day, and did righteous deeds — there will be no fear upon them from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, nor will they grieve over what they left behind them in the world.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 5, verse 70:

We had certainly taken a firm covenant from the Children of Israel in the Torah, to hear and obey, and We sent to them messengers with this. But they broke the covenant that had been taken from them, followed their own desires, and whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, they opposed him: they denied some of the messengers and killed others.

These disobedient Jews assumed that God would not punish them for their disobedience and their insolent transgression. So they pursued their desires, and they were blind to guidance, so they did not see it, and deaf to hearing the truth, so they did not benefit from it. Then God sent down His punishment upon them, and they repented, so God accepted their repentance. Then many of them became blind and deaf again, after the truth had become clear to them. God is All-Seeing of their deeds, both good and bad, and He will recompense them for them.

God Most High swears that those who said, "God is the Messiah, son of Mary," have certainly disbelieved by this statement of theirs. He informs us that the Messiah said to the Children of Israel: "Worship God alone, with no partner for Him, for I and you are equal in servitude." Indeed, whoever associates anything with God in worship, God has forbidden Paradise to him, has made the Fire his abode, and he has no helper who can rescue him from it.

Indeed, they have disbelieved who among the Christians say: "Allah is the third of three," meaning that God is composed of three things: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Do these Christians not know that there is no deity for people except one God, who neither begets nor is begotten? And if those who hold this belief do not desist from their fabrication and their lying, a painful, agonizing punishment will surely befall them because of their disbelief in Allah.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 5, verse 74:

Will these Christians not turn back to Allah, exalted is He, repent of what they have said, and ask Allah, exalted is He, for forgiveness? Allah, exalted is He, is forgiving of the sins of those who repent, and merciful to them.

The Noble Qur'an, the King Fahd Complex Commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar), on surah 5, verse 75:

The Messiah, son of Maryam (peace be upon him), is nothing but a messenger, like those messengers who came before him. And his mother had believed in the truth with a firm belief, in knowledge and in action. Both of them, like other human beings, need food. Whoever needs food in order to live cannot be a god. So reflect, O Messenger, on the state of these disbelievers. We have made clear the signs that indicate our oneness, and the falsehood of what they claim about the prophets of Allah. Yet despite this, they go astray from the truth to which We guide them. Then look at how they are turned away from the truth after this clarification.

Say, [O Messenger], to these disbelievers: "How do you associate with Allah those who cannot control harm for you or bring benefit to you? And Allah is the All-Hearing of the sayings of His servants, the All-Knowing of their conditions."

Say, O Messenger, to the Christians: Do not exceed the truth in what you believe concerning the matter of the Messiah, and do not follow your desires, just as the Jews followed their desires in matters of religion, so they fell into misguidance, led many people into disbelief in Allah, and departed from the path of uprightness to the path of error and straying.

The Exalted says that He expelled from His mercy the disbelievers among the Children of Israel, in the Scripture He revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him), which is the Zabur, and in the Scripture He revealed to Isa (peace be upon him), which is the Injil. This was because of their disobedience and their transgression against the sacred limits of Allah.

These Jews would openly commit sins and be content with them, and none of them would forbid the others from any wrong they committed. This was one of their evil deeds, and because of it they deserved to be expelled from the mercy of Allah, the Exalted.

You see, O Messenger, many of these Jews taking the polytheists as allies for themselves. Evil is what they have done, in that alliance which was the cause of Allah's wrath upon them, and of their abiding forever in the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

This is a commentary passage on Qur'an 5:81, so it is not a direct quotation to be wrapped in ﴿ ﴾ unless it appears so; the text itself is the commentary.

If they had truly believed in Allah, the Exalted, and in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and acknowledged what was revealed to him—that is, the Noble Qur'an—they would not have taken the disbelievers as companions and helpers. But many of them are rebellious against the obedience of Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 82:

You, O Messenger, will surely find the people most hostile to those who believed in you, accepted you and followed you to be the Jews, because of their obstinacy, their denial of the truth, and their rejection of the truth; and those who associated others with Allah, such as the worshippers of idols and others. And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward the Muslims to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are scholars of their religion who are ascetic, and worshippers in the monasteries who are devoted to worship, and because they are humble and do not refuse to accept the truth. These are the ones who accepted the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) and believed in it.

Among the signs of how close their affection is toward the Muslims is that a group of them [namely, the delegation from Abyssinia, when they heard the Qur'an] had their eyes overflow with tears. They became certain that it is the truth sent down from God, the Exalted. They believed in God and followed His Messenger, and they humbly asked God to honor them with the distinction of martyrdom alongside the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, before the other nations on the Day of Resurrection.

They said: "Why should we be blamed for believing in God, for affirming the truth that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought to us from God, and for following him? And we hope that our Lord will admit us along with the people who obey Him into His Garden on the Day of Resurrection?"

Then Allah rewarded them for what they said, in taking pride in their faith in Islam and in their desire to be among the righteous people: gardens beneath which rivers flow, through their palaces and trees. They will remain in them forever, never leaving them nor being moved from them. That is the reward of their goodness in word and deed.

Those who denied the Oneness of Allah and rejected the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and who denied the signs He revealed to His messengers, are the companions of the Fire, who will abide in it forever.

O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, [such as] foods, drinks, and marriage to women, thereby restricting what Allah has made broad for you. And do not transgress the limits of what Allah has forbidden. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.

Enjoy, O believers, the lawful and good things that God has bestowed upon you and granted you, and fear God by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions; for your belief in God necessitates that you be mindful of Him and watchful over your conduct.

Allah does not hold you to account, O Muslims, for what you do not intend to bind yourselves to by oaths, such as the saying of some of you: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah." Rather, He holds you to account for what you intended to bind yourselves to in your hearts. So if you do not fulfil the oath, its sin is erased by Allah through the expiation (kaffarah) that you offer, which Allah has prescribed for you: feeding ten needy persons who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need, giving each poor person half a sa' of the average food of the people of the land; or clothing them, giving each poor person what suffices for clothing according to custom; or freeing a slave from bondage. The one who swore and did not fulfil his oath has the choice among these three matters. Whoever does not find any of that must fast three days. These are the expiations for failing to fulfil your oaths. And guard your oaths, O Muslims: by refraining from swearing, or by fulfilling them if you have sworn, or by offering expiation if you do not fulfil them. Just as Allah has made clear to you the ruling on oaths and how to be released from them, so He makes clear to you the rulings of His religion, so that you may give thanks to Him for guiding you to the straight path.

O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger and act in accordance with His law! Indeed, intoxicants (al-khamr): it is every intoxicant that covers over the intellect; and gambling (al-maysir): it is games of chance, which includes wagering and the like, in which there is a consideration from both sides; and it diverts from the remembrance of Allah; and idols (al-ansab): they are the stones at which the polytheists used to slaughter, glorifying them, and whatever is set up to be worshipped, seeking nearness to it; and arrows (al-azlam): they are the arrow-shafts by which the disbelievers seek the decision (yastaqsimu) before proceeding with a matter or refraining from it. Indeed, all of that is sin, from the adornment of Satan, so keep away from these sins, that you may succeed and attain Paradise.

Satan only wants, through making sins appealing to you, to sow enmity and hatred among you because of drinking wine and playing games of chance, and to divert you from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer, by the loss of reason in drinking wine and by busying yourselves with frivolity in games of chance. So desist from that.

Obey, O believers, Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in all that you do and refrain from, and fear Allah and be mindful of Him in that. But if you turn away from obedience and do what you have been forbidden, then know that the duty of Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is only to convey the clear message.

This is a straightforward translation task. Here is the passage in English:

There is no blame upon those who believed and did righteous deeds for what they consumed of wine before its prohibition, provided that they refrain from it now, fear the wrath of Allah, believe in Him, and do righteous deeds that show their faith and their desire for the good pleasure of Allah, the Exalted. Then they increased in watchfulness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and in faith in Him, until from their certainty they worship Him as though they see Him. Indeed, Allah the Exalted loves those who have reached the station of ihsan (excellence in worship), until their faith in the unseen becomes like direct witnessing.

O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game of the land that comes within your reach in a way other than usual, such that you can take its young with no weapon and its adults with weapons, so that Allah may know, with an evident knowledge manifest to creation, who fears their Lord in the unseen, by virtue of their certainty of His perfect knowledge of them. That is by their refraining from hunting while they are in the state of ihram. Whoever transgresses his limit after this clarification and proceeds to hunt while in ihram, then he deserves a severe punishment.

O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah, or while you are within the sacred precinct (al-Haram). Whoever among you kills any kind of land game deliberately, its penalty is to slaughter an animal like what he killed from the livestock of grazing animals—camels, cattle, or sheep—after two just persons among you have judged its equivalent, and to bring it as an offering to the poor of the Haram; or, instead, to buy food with its equivalent value and give it as an offering to the poor of the Haram, half a sa' for each needy person; or to fast a day in place of each half sa' of that food. Allah has prescribed this penalty so that he may taste the consequence of his deed. As for those who committed such things before the prohibition, Allah has pardoned them. But whoever returns to the violation deliberately after the prohibition, he is exposed to Allah's retribution. Allah is Mighty, Powerful, Invincible in His dominion, and among His might is that He takes vengeance on whoever disobeys Him whenever He wills, with nothing to prevent Him from doing so.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 96:

Allah has permitted you, O Muslims, while you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state entered into for hajj or 'umrah), the game of the sea, which is what is caught from it alive, and its food, which is what is dead of it, for your benefit, whether you are residents or travelers. He has forbidden you the game of the land as long as you remain in ihram for hajj or 'umrah. Fear Allah and carry out all of His commands, and avoid all of His prohibitions, so that you may attain His great reward and be safe from His painful punishment when you are gathered for reckoning and recompense.

Almighty God bestowed a favour upon His servants by making the Sacred House, the Kaaba, a means of righteousness for their religion and security for their lives. This is so because they believed in God and His Messenger and established His obligations. He also made aggression and fighting forbidden during the Sacred Months (namely Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram and Rajab), so that no one transgresses against anyone in them. Exalted is He, He forbade the violation of the animals brought as offerings to the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) from the livestock of cattle (bahimat al-an'am), and He likewise forbade the violation of the garlands (al-qala'id), which are the animals marked with garlands as a sign that they are intended as an act of worship (nusk). This is so that you may know that God knows all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth, and among that is what He has legislated to protect His creation from one another, and that God is All-Knowing of everything, nothing being hidden from Him.
Know, O people, that Allah, exalted is He, is severe in punishment toward whoever disobeys Him, and that Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful toward whoever repents and turns back to Him.

Allah, the Exalted, explains that the duty of His Messenger (ﷺ) is the guidance of indication (*hidayat al-dalala*, showing the way) and the conveying of the message. The guidance of divine success (*hidayat al-tawfiq*) is in the hand of Allah alone. And whatever the souls of people harbor, whether they conceal it or declare it openly, of guidance or misguidance, Allah knows it.

Say, O Messenger: The corrupt and the good are not equal, in anything at all. So the disbelIever is not equal to the believer, the disobedient is not equal to the obedient, the ignorant is not equal to the knowledgeable, the innovator (mubtadi') is not equal to the one who follows the Sunnah (muttabi'), and unlawfully gotten wealth is not equal to lawful wealth, even if the abundance of the corrupt and the number of its people impress you, O human. So fear Allah, O people of sound minds, by avoiding the corrupt things and doing the good things, so that you may prosper by attaining the greatest goal, which is the pleasure of Allah, may He be exalted, and success in Paradise.

O you who have believed God and His Messenger and acted according to His law, do not ask about things concerning matters of religion about which you were not commanded anything, such as asking about matters that have not occurred, or that would entail restrictions in the law which, if you were obligated to them, would be burdensome for you. And if you ask about them during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and at the time the Qur'an is being revealed to him, they will be explained to you. But you may be obligated to them and then be unable to perform them, so God has left them as a pardon for His servants concerning them. And God is Most Forgiving toward His servants when they repent, Most Forbearing toward them, so He does not punish them when they have turned back to Him.

Indeed, a people before you asked such questions of their messengers. Then, when they were commanded to act upon them, they denied them and did not carry them out. So beware lest you become like them.

The passage is from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, commenting on Surah al-Ma'idah (5), verse 103.

God did not ordain any of what the polytheists invented concerning the cattle (bahimat al-an'am): abandoning the benefit of some of them and dedicating them to idols. These are: the bahirah, whose ear is slit when it has borne a number of litters; the saibah, which is left free for the idols; the wasilah, whose births are successively female after female; and the ham, which is the male camel when a number of camels has been sired from its loins. But the disbelievers attributed this to God, the Exalted, as a fabrication against Him. Most of the disbelievers do not distinguish truth from falsehood.

When it is said to these disbelievers who declared unlawful what God has made lawful: "Come to what God has sent down and to the Messenger," they say: "What we found our fathers doing is enough for us." Even if their fathers knew nothing and were not guided? That is, they do not understand the truth, nor do they recognize it, nor are they guided to it. So how can they follow them in such a state? For none follows them except one who is more ignorant than they and further astray from the way.

O you who have believed, God and His Messenger, and have acted by His law: commit yourselves to acting in obedience to God and avoiding His disobedience, and persist in that even if people do not respond to you. If you do this, then the straying of those who have strayed will not harm you when you adhere to the path of uprightness and enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. To God is your return, all of you, in the Hereafter, and He will inform you of your deeds and recompense you for them.

O you who have believed: when death approaches one of you, let there be a bequest witnessed by two just men from among yourselves, or two others from outside your own community if none of your own is available while you are traveling in the land and the affliction of death befalls you. If you have doubt about their testimony, detain them after the prayer, that is, the prayer of the Muslims, especially the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). They shall swear by Allah, saying: "We will not sell our oath for any worldly gain, even if it concerns a near relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah that is with us. Indeed, if we did that, we would be among the sinners."

If the heirs of the deceased discover that the two witnesses mentioned have committed treachery in the testimony or the bequest, then two of the deceased's heirs shall take their place in testifying, and they shall swear by God: "Our true testimony is more deserving of acceptance than their false testimony, and we have not transgressed the truth in our testimony. Indeed, if we were to transgress and testify falsely, we would be among the wrongdoers who exceed the limits of God."

That ruling, when there is doubt about the two witnesses who swore after the prayer and their testimony is therefore not accepted, is closer to bringing the witnesses to give their testimony in its true form, out of fear of the punishment of the Hereafter, or out of apprehension that a false oath may be rejected by the rightful claimants after they have sworn, so that the liar whose oath was rejected is exposed in this world at the time his treachery becomes apparent. ﴿And fear Allah, O people, and be mindful of Him,﴾ lest you swear falsely, or use your oaths to seize unlawful property, ﴿and listen,﴾ to what you are being admonished with. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people,﴾ those who go outside His obedience.

Remember, O people, the Day of Resurrection, the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers, peace be upon them, and will ask them about the response of their nations to them when they called them to monotheism. They will answer: "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing of the unseen." We do not know what is in the hearts of people, nor what they innovated after us. Indeed, You are the All-Knower of everything, whether hidden or manifest.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 5, verse 110:

When Allah says on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, [so that] you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and when I taught you writing, wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [what was] like the form of a bird by My permission, then you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission; and when you brought out the dead by My permission﴾. Among these favours upon Jesus is that Allah strengthened him and aided him with Jibril (peace be upon him). He spoke to the people while still an infant, before the time of speech, and he called them to Allah when he was grown, his strength having matured and his youth having been completed, by what Allah revealed to him of monotheism. Among them is that Allah Most High taught him writing and calligraphy without a teacher, and granted him the power of understanding and perception, and taught him the Torah that He sent down to Musa (peace be upon him), and the Gospel that was sent down to him as guidance for mankind. Among these favours is that he would shape from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathe into that form, and it would become a bird by the permission of Allah. Among them is that he would heal one born blind so that he sees, and heal the leper so that his skin returns whole, by the permission of Allah. Among them is that he would call upon Allah to give life to the dead, so that they rise from their graves alive; and all of that is by the will and permission of Allah Most High. These are dazzling miracles that confirm the prophethood of Jesus (peace be upon him). Then the Almighty and Majestic reminds him of His favour upon him when He restrained the Children of Israel when they resolved to kill him, although he had brought them the clear miracles indicating his prophethood. Those among them who disbelieved said: "What Jesus brought of clear proofs is manifest magic."

"And remember, O Jesus, My favor upon you, when I inspired and cast into the hearts of a group of your close companions that they should believe in the Oneness of God and in your prophethood. So they said, 'We have believed, O our Lord, so bear witness that we are submissive to You and compliant with Your command.'"

And remember when the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, is your Lord able to send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven?" His answer was that he commanded them to fear the punishment of God, the Exalted, if they were believers with true faith.

The Disciples said: "We wish to eat from the table-spread, so that our hearts may be at rest by seeing it, and that we may know with certainty that you have spoken truly concerning your prophethood, and that we may be among those who bear witness to this sign: that God sent it down as a proof against us for His oneness and His power over whatever He wills, and as a proof for you of the truth of your prophethood."

Jesus, son of Mary, answered the request of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun), so he called upon his Lord, may He be exalted, saying: "Our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from heaven, which will be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You (O Allah) of Your oneness and of the truthfulness of my prophethood. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers."

God the Exalted said: "Indeed, I shall send down the table spread with food upon you. Whoever among you disbelieves after its descent, I shall surely punish him with a punishment such that I shall not punish anyone else among the worlds with it." And the table (al-ma'idah) was indeed sent down, as Allah had promised.

And mention when Allah says on the Day of Resurrection: "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He will answer, glorifying Allah above any partner: "It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would already know it, for nothing is hidden from You. You know what is within my self, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of all unseen things."

Isa (peace be upon him) said: "My Lord, I did not say to them except what You revealed to me and commanded me to convey: that You alone are to be worshipped and that worship is to be devoted to You alone. I was a witness over them and over their deeds and their words while I was among them. But when You caused me to complete my term upon the earth and raised me up to heaven alive, You were the One watching over their inner thoughts, and You are Witness over all things; nothing is hidden from You on earth or in heaven."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful... (not needed). Here is the translation:

"If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants—and You know best their circumstances—You do with them what You will, in Your justice. And if You forgive them, by Your mercy, those among them who have come with the causes of forgiveness, then indeed You are the Mighty, whom none can overcome, the Wise in Your management and Your command. And this verse is a praise of Allah—Exalted is He—for His wisdom, His justice, and the perfection of His knowledge."

God said to Jesus, peace be upon him, on the Day of Resurrection: "This is the Day of Recompense, on which the sincerity of those who affirmed the Oneness of their Lord benefits them: their monotheism (tawhid), their submission to His law, and their truthfulness in their intentions, their words and their deeds. For them are Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, so He accepts their good deeds, and they are pleased with Him for what He has given them of His abundant reward. That recompense and that pleasure from Him toward them is the great triumph."
Belonging to Allah alone, without partner, is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He, glory be to Him, is able to do all things; nothing can overpower Him.
